question.text: Attucks was the first person killed in this event on March 5, 1770. Paul Revere made an engraving showing this event, in which five colonists died in Massachusetts' capital.
question.clue: The engraving The Fruits of Arbitrary Power by Henry Pelham depicts this event by showing a linear arrangement of eight men standing outside a custom house.

swap.text: The Battles of Long Island and Saratoga occurred during this war, which was ended when the French and American forces surrounded Cornwallis at Yorktown.
swap.answerHtml: American Revolutionary War [or American Revolution; or American War of Independence]
swap.clue: In the leadup to this war, the term "virtual representation" described tariffs passed by Charles Townshend.

question.leadin: There are eighty-five of these in total, and they were written to gain support for replacing the Articles of Confederation.
question.text: Name this set of documents, written under a famous pseudonym, that proposed a strong republic instead of the powerless government the Articles of Confederation created.
question.clue: A group of men with "neither FORCE nor WILL" is the subject of its seventy-eighth part.

swap.leadin: This work advocated the framing of a Continental Charter by delegates from each colony.
swap.text: Name this work, which also argued that an island ruling a continent is ridiculous, a 1776 pamphlet arguing for American independence.
swap.clue: Another chapter of this work claims that a certain monarch did little but "make war and give away places".

question.text: The Anti-Federalist Papers were partially written by this Virginia politician who staunchly supported states' rights and supposedly declared, "I smell a rat!" during the Constitutional convention.
question.clue: The opening of Daniel Webster's "Seventh of March" address resembles this politician's desire to be seen as "not a Virginian, but an American" in an earlier speech.

swap.text: The first openly trans student at Harvard, Alex Myers, wrote a history of Deborah Sampson, a woman who secretly served under this general. This first Secretary of War was Washington's chief artillery officer and now names a fort that defends the United States Bullion Depository.
swap.clue: In that role, this general led such men as du Plessis, whose troops almost single handedly repulsed a British advance at the Battle of Monmouth.

question.text: Warren sent Revere and Dawes to evacuate John Hancock and this man from Lexington. This man had earlier called a meeting at Faneuil ["FAN-yool"] Hall that sparked an attack on the Dartmouth.
question.clue: Thomas Gage exempted John Hancock and this person when Gage offered to pardon people who laid down their arms during the Battles of Lexington and Concord.

swap.leadin: This man replaced Thomas Gage as commander-in-chief of North America for the British army and led it during the first part of the American Revolution.
swap.text: Name this general who captured the colonial capital of Philadelphia after defeating George Washington's army at the Battle of Brandywine Creek.
swap.clue: Though he won the Battle of Brandywine to capture Philadelphia, his 1778 resignation led to his replacement by Henry Clinton.

question.leadin: Name these heroes of the American Revolution.
question.text: Marion teamed up with this guy in 1781 at the Battle of Eutaw Springs. This master strategist and leader of the southern army earlier fought at Princeton and Brandywine.
question.clue: While working for this person's widow at the Mulberry Grove plantation outside Savannah, Eli Whitney invented the cotton gin.

swap.leadin: Name these people from the life of Aaron Burr.
swap.text: In 1776, Burr was appointed aide to this general, who said "Don't fire until you see the whites of their eyes" at Bunker Hill.
swap.clue: He was second-in-command to Artemas Ward in the Army of Observation, and along with Ward, Philip Schuyler and Charles Lee, was one of four major generals appointed by the Continental Congress in 1775.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Isaiah Thomas.
question.text: In 1771, this governor of Massachusetts tried to shut down Thomas's newspaper, the Massachusetts Spy. Earlier, this man's house was ransacked by a mob protesting the Stamp Act.
question.clue: For actually leaking this politician's letters, Benjamin Franklin was removed from his office as Postmaster General, although the public fixated on this administrator's suggestion to abridge "English liberties."

swap.leadin: This battle was sparked by a British plan to fortify Dorchester Heights.
swap.text: Name this misleadingly named early Revolutionary War battle, a pyrrhic victory for the British. During this battle, a commander apocryphally told his soldiers not to shoot until they saw the "whites of their eyes".
swap.answerHtml: Battle of Bunker Hill [accept Battle of Breed's Hill]
swap.clue: Men killed during this battle included a physician from the Committee of Correspondence, Joseph Warren, who appears in the painting of this battle by John Trumbull.

question.leadin: In response to these laws, John Dickinson wrote that Americans will be made "as abject slaves as France and Poland can [show]" in his Letters from a Farmer in Pennsylvania.
question.text: Name these acts that taxed goods like paper, glass, and tea through an American Board of Customs Commissioners. They were named for the minister who proposed them in 1767.
question.clue: The "Massachusetts Circular" letter was written by Samuel Adams in response to this program, and these acts led to the seizure of a sloop owned by John Hancock, the Liberty.

swap.leadin: The victorious force under Daniel Morgan was bolstered by the Overmountain men, who had fought at Musgrove Hill and King's Mountain.
swap.text: Identify this Revolutionary War battle fought between the Broad and Pacolet Rivers, which saw a defeat for Banastre Tarleton.
swap.clue: Colonial soldiers in the first two lines of this battle were ordered by Daniel Morgan to fire at British officers before falling back, which made Banastre Tarleton think they were retreating.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Lake Champlain's storied military history.
question.text: This fort on the southern end of Lake Champlain was captured by Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys in an early Revolutionary War action.
question.clue: This fort's location near Lake Champlain made it useful in monitoring trade routes between New York and Canada.

swap.leadin: Two members of this family were nicknamed the "Adam and Eve of Virginia" because of their dozens of prominent descendants, including Thomas Jefferson and Robert E. Lee.
swap.text: Name this planter family. Peyton, a member of this family, was the first president of the Continental Congress, while his nephew Edmund was the first U.S. attorney general.
swap.clue: A third member of this family prosecuted Samuel Chase and led the Tertium Quids.

question.text: Some scholars believe that this African-born author helped write that petition. Her other political works include the poem "To His Excellency, General Washington."
question.clue: This first published African American writer of many poems praising men named George, such as King George III and George Washington.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Committees of Correspondence.
swap.text: Together with Benjamin Franklin and Dr. Arthur Lee, this Connecticut-born man became the first U.S. diplomat sent abroad when he went to France as a secret agent. He had been sent by the so-called Secret Committee, and met with the Comte de Vergennes in 1776 to secure munitions.
swap.clue: In 1776 this man was sent as the colonial representative to France, and convinced Lafayette to fight for the colonial cause. That same year he was joined by Benjamin Franklin and Arthur Lee and the three negotiated a formal treaty of alliance with France in 1778.

question.text: One of the reasons Burgoyne had to surrender at Saratoga was that this general failed to come from New York in time to reinforce him. He led forces that captured Charleston, then put those forces under the charge of Charles Cornwallis before returning to England.
question.clue: This British general served as supreme commander of British forces in America from 1778 to 1781, replacing William Howe. He led the army that forced Benjamin Lincoln to surrender Charleston.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about an American frontiersman.
swap.text: This man took part in the 1784 settlers' revolt against North Carolina. He was elected as the first governor of the state of Franklin and later served as the first governor of Tennessee.
swap.clue: Along with James Robertson, this Virginian founded the Watauga settlement and he would later lead 250 frontiersmen to victory at King's Mountain.
